title: Account retention metrics playlist and SLI action checklist
content:
Purpose:
Quick working reference for QBR-facing metric definitions and the minimal action table we use in customer reviews. A lightweight, 'playlist' view: definitions + how we measure + what to present (one row per metric). Designed for cyclical QBR prep (30/60/90 day windows).

Notes to self (formatting intent):
- Keep each metric entry: name | short definition | calc formula | source | window | actionable threshold | suggested CS talking points.
- Include a small table with synthetic examples (to show expected scale).
- Add one-liner remediation play for common outliers.

Metric entries:
1) Median P50 response latency (ms)
- Definition: median end-to-end time from request accepted to first token returned for text gen API.
- Formula: median(token_start_time - request_received_time) over N requests.
- Source: hosted-api request logs (trace_id) + traces service.
- Window: 7d / 30d for trends.
- Thresholds & actions: <= 250ms green; 250-500ms amber (investigate batching spikes); >500ms red (route to higher-tier model or scale pool).
- CS talking points: correlate to recent peak hours; show impact on perceived interactivity.

2) P95 tail latency (ms)
- Definition: 95th percentile of end-to-end request latency. Important for worst-case experience.
- Formula: 95th percentile(token_end_time - request_received_time).
- Source: traces + telemetry.
- Window: 1d / 7d rolling.
- Thresholds & actions: set customer-specific SLOs in dashboard; if breach, propose canary rollback to smaller context or autoscale step-up.

3) Uptime (availability) - route-level
- Definition: percent of successful responses (2xx) served within target latency SLO for the route.
- Formula: successful_within_slo / total_requests * 100
- Source: route-metrics + error budget service.
- Window: 30d and 90d.
- Threshold & action: <99.9% -> open incident review, check fallback policy (model-variant fallback).

4) Cost per effective token ($/k token)
- Definition: allocated cost (compute + infra) divided by effective tokens billed (excluding retries). Normalized per 1k tokens.
- Formula: (gpu_cost + infra_admin_cost + cache_cost) / (total_billed_tokens/1000)
- Source: billing export + infra cost bucket per project.
- Window: monthly + last quarter.
- Threshold & actions: rising >10% QoQ -> run optimize playbook (quantize, reduce seq length, caching policy).

5) Cache hit rate (prefix / kv hits)
- Definition: percent of requests served with at least one cached prefix or KV reuse that avoided full model compute.
- Formula: requests_with_cache_hit / total_requests * 100
- Source: serving-runtime cache logs + trace annotations.
- Window: 7d / 30d.
- Threshold & actions: <20% for conversational workloads -> suggest prompt templating and fixed prefixes; for retrieval-heavy workloads target 40%+.

Action table (condensed)
- Metric | Red trigger | Immediate CS ask | Runbook
- P95 latency | >800ms | Ask for recent query samples + traffic spike times | Scale pool + check model selection logs
- Uptime | <99.5% (30d) | Request incident timeline & SAML change logs | Escalate to SRE; enable fallback routes
- Cost/token | +15% QoQ | Review batch sizes, model variants used | Run Optimize checklist (batching, quant, caching)
- Cache hit | <15% | Get prompt samples and bot flow | Recommend prefix standardization + memory policies

Sample KPI table (synthetic):
- account: acme-inc | p50: 210ms | p95: 420ms | uptime30d: 99.92% | cost_per_k: $0.64 | cache_hit: 33%
- account: beta-shop | p50: 480ms | p95: 1200ms | uptime30d: 99.30% | cost_per_k: $1.40 | cache_hit: 8%

Reporting + visualizations to prepare for QBR:
- 1 slide: trend sparkline (30d) for p50/p95/cost_per_k and a single-line note of root cause if degraded.
- 1 slide: distribution chart of latency by route (heatmap).
- 1 appendix slide: 3 example slow traces + payload size + model param.

Quick measurement snippets (PSUEDO SQL-ish):
- p50 latency: SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 50) FROM traces WHERE account_id = :id AND ts > now()-interval '30 days';
- cache hit rate: SELECT sum(cache_hit)::float / count(*) FROM requests WHERE account_id = :id AND ts > now()-interval '7 days';
- cost per k: join billing_lineitems on project_id and sum(cost)/ (sum(tokens)/1000)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Agree on default windows for different customer tiers (S1 vs S3).
- Add standard phrasing for CS to explain cost/token variance to finance teams.
- Find canonical query for prefix vs KV cache distinction in logs.

Intended next steps:
- Share with Jordan + Priya for critique (ask for threshold sanity checks)
- Add examples exported from two customer accounts (one high cache, one low cache)
- Turn this into a one-page QBR checklist slide for CS playbooks repo.

Notes: keep this doc short and pragmatic. This is a tactical reference for CS engineers prepping QBRs — not the canonical instrumentation spec (that lives in infra/observability).
